optical_type: Spherical cell body microlens
genetic_toolkit: Prokaryotic biliprotein + Type IV pili
plain_title: A single bacterium uses its own round body as a tiny lens
plain_text: Three-micrometer cyanobacteria focus incoming light onto the far wall of their own spherical cell and pull themselves toward brighter water with microscopic grappling hooks.
note: Demonstrates physical micro-optics in prokaryotes 2+ billion years before eyes.

optical_type: Shaded carotenoid Bragg-reflector eyespot
genetic_toolkit: Chloroplast carotenoid stack + Ca2+ flagellar current
plain_title: An orange eyespot steers two flagella within milliseconds
plain_text: Green algae back a patch of channelrhodopsin ion pores with layered orange pigment mirrors so a spinning cell tells exactly where sunlight comes from—the same protein now used in optogenetics.
source: Foster & Smyth 1980; Nagel et al. 2002; Kreimer 2009
note: Nilsson Stage 1 directional shading inside a single eukaryotic cell.

optical_type: Subcellular organelle lens + plastid retinal body
genetic_toolkit: Endosymbiotic mitochondrion 'cornea' + red-algal plastid 'retina'
plain_title: A single-celled plankton builds a miniature camera eye out of organelles
plain_text: Predatory warnowiid dinoflagellates repurpose mitochondria as a cornea and a captured red-algal plastid as a polarized retina—a lens eye inside one microscopic cell.
source: Gavelis et al. 2015; Hayakawa et al. 2015
note: Most complex known subcellular optical structure.

milestone: Animal c-opsin & r-opsin divergence (ambient light patch)
optical_type: Unshaded ambient photoreceptor patch
genetic_toolkit: Ancestral PaxB/Pax6 + Six3/Rx transcription network
plain_title: First animal opsins split into our rods-and-cones family and the insect family
plain_text: Before the Cambrian, early animals split vitamin-A opsins into two sister branches—ciliary opsins that became vertebrate retinas and rhabdomeric opsins that became insect eyes and our circadian clock cells.
source: Arendt et al. 2004; Feuda et al. 2012; Nilsson 2013
note: Nilsson Class I non-directional irradiance sensing.

optical_type: Concave melanin-shaded pigment cup
genetic_toolkit: Sine oculis / Otx / Eyes absent cup specification
plain_title: Curving a pigment sheet into a cup gives worms left-right shadow vision
plain_text: By indenting a flat receptor patch into a dark cup just 80 micrometers across, flatworms tell which directions are dark shelter versus perilous open light without needing a lens.
note: Nilsson Class II directional photoreception (~20% of the Nilsson-Pelger path).

milestone: 24-eye graded-index rhopalial vision without a central brain
optical_type: Graded-index spherical protein lens (8 lens + 16 pit/slit eyes)
genetic_toolkit: PaxB + J-crystallin enzyme co-option
plain_title: A brainless box jellyfish carries 24 eyes—eight with genuine graded lenses
plain_text: Dangling four sensory clubs around its bell, the mangrove box jellyfish looks simultaneously upward through Snell's window to navigate tree canopies and horizontally to dodge roots, all without a central brain.
source: Nilsson et al. 2005; Garm et al. 2011; Piatigorsky et al. 1989
note: Proves aberration-free graded lenses can evolve ahead of centralized brains.

optical_type: Open seawater-flushed variable pinhole chamber
genetic_toolkit: Conserved Pax6 pinhole arrest (missing lens induction)
plain_title: Nautilus freezes evolution halfway—showing the brightness-versus-sharpness trap
plain_text: A chambered nautilus builds a ten-millimeter eye with four million receptors but no lens: narrowing its 1-mm pinhole sharpens shapes yet starves the retina of photons, demonstrating why true lenses swept the seas.
note: Living demonstration of the physical pinhole trade-off.

optical_type: Stalked apposition compound eye (>16,700 hexagonal lenses)
genetic_toolkit: Pax6/eyeless ommatidial lattice
plain_title: 16,700 lenses on stalks ignite the Cambrian arms race
plain_text: Three-centimeter fossilized eyes from Kangaroo Island show Anomalocaris packed more than 16,700 lenses per eye—turning sunlit Cambrian waters into a lethal visual hunting ground.
note: Emu Bay Shale phosphatized compound eye fossils.

optical_type: Birefringent single-crystal CaCO3 Huygens-Descartes doublet
genetic_toolkit: Biomineralized c-axis oriented calcite + intralensar bowl
plain_title: Trilobites grew mineral crystal lenses obeying Descartes' 1637 optical law
plain_text: Alone in animal history, trilobites ground their lenses out of pure calcite crystal; phacopid trilobites fused a wavy upper calcite crystal to a magnesium-rich lower bowl to cancel spherical aberration underwater.
note: Schizochroal doublet lenses match Descartes (1637) and Huygens (1690) exact aplanatic curves.

optical_type: Coarse apposition cylinder-lens compound eye with eccentric-cell inhibitory plexus
opsin_class: Visible + UV r-opsins + circadian efferent brain gain
genetic_toolkit: Hartline-Ratliff lateral-inhibition Mach-band equation
plain_title: Horseshoe crabs revealed the universal math of edge detection
plain_text: Recording from the 1,000-facet eye of Limulus won H. Keffer Hartline the Nobel Prize: every lit facet quiets its neighbors, sharpening dim underwater silhouettes—and doubling sensitivity at night on a clock signal from the brain.
note: Living fossil benchmark where lateral inhibition was first formulated mathematically.

optical_type: Concave square-guanine multilayer mirror + dual stacked retinas
genetic_toolkit: Pax6 + tiled square guanine photonic crystals
plain_title: Scallops watch for starfish with 200 biological telescope mirrors
plain_text: Instead of focusing light chiefly with a lens, each blue eye along a scallop's shell bounces light off a curved mosaic of microscopic square guanine crystals onto two stacked retinas, just like the James Webb telescope.
note: Remarkably expresses BOTH r-opsin and c-opsin on two separate retinas in the same eye.

optical_type: Trinocular compound eye with 6-row scanning hyperspectral midband
opsin_class: 12-16 r-opsins + MAA UV filters + carotenoid intrarhabdomal filters
genetic_toolkit: Massive r-opsin tandem duplication + microvillar quarter-wave retarder
plain_title: Sixteen color channels and circular polarization—turning color into a hardware lookup
plain_text: Rather than burning heavy brainpower comparing three cones, a peacock mantis shrimp sweeps a six-row midband of twelve color receptors, four UV channels and quarter-wave circular polarization plates across reef prey.
source: Marshall & Oberwinkler 1999; Chiou et al. 2008; Thoen et al. 2014
note: World record spectral + full-Stokes polarization hardware dimensionality.

optical_type: Panoramic apposition eye with dorsal acute 'foveal' band
opsin_class: 5 ventral/dorsal specialized r-opsins (UV/blue sky vs broad ventral)
genetic_toolkit: Lamina predictive coding + STMD small-target neurons
plain_title: 28,000 facets and 300 frames a second—the physical ceiling of compound eyes
plain_text: A hunting dragonfly wraps nearly its entire head in 28,000 facets and refreshes light up to 300 times a second—five times faster than human vision—hitting 95% mid-air capture success.
source: Futahashi et al. 2015; Laughlin et al. 1998; Olberg et al. 2000
note: Diffraction limits insect compound eyes: matching human 60-cpd acuity would require a 1-meter-wide compound eye!

milestone: Refracting superposition single-photon night compound eye
optical_type: Refracting superposition clear-zone compound eye (hundreds of facets sum onto 1 rhabdom)
genetic_toolkit: Graded-index crystalline cones + clear-zone summation
plain_title: Night hawkmoths pool hundreds of lenses to see true color by starlight
plain_text: Humans go completely color-blind under starlight, yet elephant hawkmoths open a clear optical zone inside their eyes so hundreds of facets focus onto one receptor, hover-feeding on colored flowers at 0.0001 lux.
note: 1,000x brighter retinal image than apposition compound eyes.

optical_type: Tiered rhabdom apposition eye with perirhabdomal red/yellow filtering pigments
opsin_class: UV, violet, blue, double-green, red & broadband r-opsins
genetic_toolkit: Co-evolved angiosperm petal reflectance + host-leaf polarization
plain_title: Swallowtail butterflies see six color bands from ultraviolet to deep red
plain_text: Co-evolving with flowering plants, swallowtail butterflies pack eight photoreceptors of six spectral classes into every single facet, spotting a 1-nanometer hue shift better than the human eye.
note: Demonstrates true behavioral tetrachromacy/hexachromacy in pollinating insects.

milestone: Miniature Pitot-tube telephoto scanning camera eyes
optical_type: Corneal lens + movable boomerang pitot-tube 4-tier retina + 6 secondary wide-angle eyes
genetic_toolkit: Tiered chromatic-aberration rangefinder retina
plain_title: Jumping spiders beat insect diffraction with tiny internal telescope tubes
plain_text: Ditching compound facets for twin forward telescope tubes whose four-layered retinas swing behind fixed corneas, a five-millimeter jumping spider achieves cat-like sharpness and judges jump distance from chromatic blur.
source: Land 1969; Nagata et al. 2012; Zurek et al. 2015
note: Baltic amber salticid fossils (~44-50 Ma) + depth-from-defocus physics.

optical_type: Spherical graded-index water lens + inverted 5-class opsin retina
opsin_class: Ancestral 5-class c-opsins (LWS, SWS1, SWS2, RH2, RH1) + melanopsin
genetic_toolkit: Pax6 + 2R genome duplication + neural-crest sclera/iris
plain_title: Early fish already carried five cone/rod pigments and a five-layer retina
plain_text: Half a billion years ago, jawless fish already built our full camera-eye blueprint: a spherical Matthiessen graded-index lens focusing onto a five-layer retina with four color cones plus dim-light rhodopsin.
source: Lamb et al. 2007; Collin et al. 2003; Shu et al. 2003
note: Solves Darwin's 'organ of extreme perfection' via early chordate embryology & fossils.

milestone: Split tubular upward lens + downward crystal-mirror eye
optical_type: Dorsal f/0.9 lens tube + lateral guanine-plate curved mirror diverticulum
genetic_toolkit: Rotated guanine crystal-plate image-forming vertebrate mirror
plain_title: The only known vertebrate that forms focused images with a mirror
plain_text: Living a kilometer down, the brownsnout spookfish points twin lens tubes straight up at faint sunlight while curving mirrored side pouches downward to focus bioluminescent flashes from below.
note: Unique vertebrate reflective image-forming optic.

optical_type: 90-mm spherical Matthiessen lens + 1.5-W retro-orbital heater muscle
genetic_toolkit: Modified superior-rectus muscle losing sarcomeres for SERCA heat
plain_title: Warming a basketball-sized fish eye boosts motion speed tenfold in cold depths
plain_text: In 6 °C deep water an unheated fish retina blurs past 4 Hz; by pumping 28 °C blood from a modified eye muscle, a swordfish boosts retinal flicker resolution above 40 Hz to ambush fast squid.
note: Direct demonstration of temperature Q10 on photoreceptor kinetics.

milestone: Adaptive eye loss saving 15% of juvenile energy
optical_type: Embryonic lens apoptosis & sunken vestigial cyst (vs 3.2-mm surface eye)
genetic_toolkit: Downregulated shh/Pax6 eye field + expanded lateral-line/taste buds
plain_title: Why blind cavefish ditch their eyes: dark current costs 15% of resting energy
plain_text: Even in pitch darkness, vertebrate rods pump sodium ions nonstop; direct oxygen measurements prove Mexican cavefish evolved blindness not by accident, but to save 15% of juvenile energy in food-poor caves.
source: Moran et al. 2015; Gore et al. 2018
note: Critical energetic control proving the steep metabolic cost of keeping a retina alive.

milestone: Dorsal crocodile-like air-interface cornea (1,000,000x volume leap)
optical_type: Curved air-cornea (~43 D refractive power) + flatter crystalline lens
genetic_toolkit: Corneal refractive takeover + tear glands/eyelids
plain_title: Lifting eyes above water multiplied visible space a millionfold
plain_text: Underwater, even clear lakes absorb and scatter light within meters; fossils show lobe-finned fish tripled eye-socket size *before* walking on land, seeing 100 times farther and scanning a million times more volume.
note: Optical physics + Devonian tetrapodomorph orbit morphometrics.

optical_type: 264-mm bony-ringed f/1.0 mesopelagic photon-bucket camera eye
genetic_toolkit: 14-plate ossified sclerotic ring resisting 500-m dive pressure
plain_title: Jurassic sea reptiles grew dinner-plate eyes to spot giant squid silhouettes
plain_text: Fossil bony eye rings over 26 centimeters across gave Jurassic ichthyosaurs an f/1.0 aperture a hundred times larger in area than a human pupil, catching single bioluminescent flashes half a kilometer down.
source: Motani et al. 1999; Nilsson et al. 2012
note: Largest fossilized eye in geological history.

optical_type: 270-mm spherical graded lens + 90-mm pupil + everted (non-blind-spot) retina
genetic_toolkit: Convergent S-crystallin (glutathione S-transferase) + everted retina
plain_title: Why giant squid grow 27-centimeter eyes: spotting hunting sperm whales at 120 meters
plain_text: Optical modeling proves eyes past nine centimeters stop helping for small prey—giant squid pay for basketball-sized eyes specifically to see the faint glowing plankton wake stirred by diving sperm whales.
note: Largest living eye on Earth; convergent camera eye with zero blind spot.

milestone: Nocturnal bottleneck rod-rich duplex retina & tapetum
optical_type: Wide-aperture slit/round pupil + retroreflective tapetum lucidum + 97% rod retina
opsin_class: 2 cones (SWS1 + LWS; lost RH2 & SWS2!) + high-gain RH1 rod
genetic_toolkit: Nrl transcription factor converting cones -> rods + tapetal riboflavin/zinc mirror
plain_title: 140 million years in the dark cost mammals two color cones—and perfected night vision
plain_text: Hiding from daytime dinosaurs, ancestral mammals threw away two of the four vertebrate color opsins, converted most cones into single-photon rods, and added an eye-shine mirror behind the retina.
source: Walls 1942; Davies et al. 2012; Field & Rieke 2002
note: Explains why dogs, deer and red-green color-blind humans are dichromats.

optical_type: Keyhole-snout 55-deg stereo camera eyes (~130 mm globe)
genetic_toolkit: Keyhole postorbital bar + sclerotic ring
plain_title: Unlike Jurassic Park's myth, T. rex had 13-centimeter hawk-grade stereo eyes
plain_text: Periscoping over a narrowed snout, Tyrannosaurus overlapped both thirteen-centimeter eyes across 55 degrees—wider than a modern hawk—potentially resolving prey several kilometers away whether moving or completely still.
note: Perimetric stereo-field reconstruction on T. rex skulls.

milestone: Independent 180-deg turrets + negative-power Galilean telephoto lens
optical_type: Positive high-power cornea + concave DIVERGING (-12 D) crystalline lens
genetic_toolkit: Unique vertebrate negative lens magnifying retinal image & measuring exact tongue range by accommodation!
plain_title: Chameleons judge tongue-strike distance with a single eye using a Galilean negative lens
plain_text: Uniquely among vertebrates, a chameleon's lens *diverges* light behind a strongly curved cornea like a Galilean telescope, magnifying insects and measuring exact strike distance from lens focus alone.
note: Only vertebrate known to judge absolute range monocularly via accommodation effort.

milestone: Tubular f/1.1 rod-packed acoustic-aligned night raptor eye
optical_type: Elongated bony-ringed f/1.13 tubular eye locked in skull (270-deg neck rotation)
opsin_class: 95% high-gain RH1 rods (lost UV SWS1 cone)
genetic_toolkit: Optic tectum co-registering 3D facial-disc sound map with stereo visual map
plain_title: Barn owls fuse tubular f/1.1 starlight eyes with an asymmetric 3D sound map
plain_text: Trading away color and daytime sharpness for an f/1.1 light-gathering tube five times brighter than a human eye, a barn owl locks visual and asymmetric ear maps onto the same midbrain neurons.
note: Classic neuroethology model of multimodal visual-auditory map alignment.

optical_type: Pecten-nourished avascular retina + 4 cones with colored carotenoid oil microlenses
genetic_toolkit: Carotenoid spectral band-pass oil droplets + vascular pecten oculi
plain_title: Songbirds see ultraviolet plumage, 145 frames a second, and Earth's magnetic field
plain_text: Every bird cone places a microscopic ruby, amber or clear oil droplet directly in front of its opsin to sharpen color separation—while migratory robins sense Earth's magnetic tilt via quantum spin pairs in retinal cryptochrome.
source: Vorobyev et al. 1998; Bostrom et al. 2016; Xu et al. 2021
note: Combines 145-Hz aerial flicker speed with 4-dimensional color space and magnetoreception.

optical_type: Tubular 35-mm eye + deep convex-pit telephoto fovea (1M cones/mm2!) + temporal stereo fovea
genetic_toolkit: Refractive foveal pit magnifying central image ~1.45x onto 1.6-um cones
plain_title: 140 cycles per degree: the sharpest biological eyesight ever measured
plain_text: Packing a million cones per square millimeter inside a magnifying foveal pit—five times denser than a human fovea—Australia's wedge-tailed eagle spots a rabbit moving across grass more than three kilometers below.
source: Reymond 1985; Mitkus et al. 2017; Caves et al. 2018
note: Biological Nyquist diffraction ceiling for terrestrial vertebrate eyes.

milestone: Each eyeball heavier than its entire brain
optical_type: 16-mm f/0.85 giant immobile tubular globes (rotated via 180-deg owl-like neck)
genetic_toolkit: Secondary nocturnal adaptation AFTER losing tapetum lucidum
plain_title: Why tarsiers grow eyes heavier than their brains: losing the mammal night mirror
plain_text: Because daytime early primates lost the reflective tapetum behind the retina, tarsiers that returned to night hunting could only catch enough starlight by inflating each eyeball past the weight of their own brain.
note: Classic proof of Dollo's law / evolutionary contingency in eye anatomy.

milestone: Duplicated X-linked M/L opsin + stereo fovea
optical_type: Forward-facing 20-mm stereo camera eyes + all-cone central foveola
opsin_class: S (420 nm) + duplicated M (530 nm) & L (560 nm) c-opsins + RH1
genetic_toolkit: Unequal X-chromosome opsin crossover + midget 1:1 foveal private-line RGCs
plain_title: A duplicated opsin gene splits red from green across leafy canopies
plain_text: Around 25–30 million years ago, our Old World monkey ancestors duplicated their long-wave opsin on the X chromosome, lighting up ripe fruit, tender reddish leaves and bare-skin social blushes.
source: Nathans et al. 1986; Surridge et al. 2003; Changizi et al. 2006
note: Molecular clock of catarrhine OPN1MW/OPN1LW tandem duplication.

optical_type: 43-diopter cornea + accommodating 20-D crystalline lens + 200k/mm2 foveola
opsin_class: S/M/L cones + 120M single-photon RH1 rods + ipRGC melanopsin
genetic_toolkit: 5-layer ~30-channel RGC feature bank + exposed white sclera for cooperative gaze
plain_title: 126 million receptors compressed 114-fold into 30 parallel movies before the brain
plain_text: Each human eye catches single photons in starlight and reads fine print in noon glare (a ten-billion-fold span), while five retinal neuron layers compress a gigabit of raw light into ~8.75 megabits/s of edges, motion and color—wrapped in a uniquely white sclera so companions see where we look.
source: Curcio et al. 1990; Koch et al. 2006; Tinsley et al. 2016; Kobayashi & Kohshima 1997
note: Pair total = 252M photoreceptors, 2.4M optic nerve fibers, ~45 mW ocular ATP + ~4.5 W visual cortex.

optical_type: 7-element aspheric f/1.78 lens + 3D-stacked back-illuminated pinned photodiode array
genetic_toolkit: 3-nm Cu-Cu wafer-bonded ISP + multi-frame HDR + CNN demosaicing
plain_title: Five billion pocket CMOS cameras surpass human pixel count—yet lose on single-frame dynamic range
plain_text: Modern stacked silicon sensors capture 200 million pixels at 240 frames a second with 85% quantum efficiency, but still need multi-exposure computational HDR to approach the ten-log-unit dynamic range of a living retina.
note: Over 15 billion CMOS image sensors manufactured globally.

optical_type: Per-pixel asynchronous log-contrast change detector (no frames!)
genetic_toolkit: Biomimetic peripheral-retina transient Y-cell architecture
plain_title: Event cameras ditch video frames so every pixel fires only when brightness changes
plain_text: Modeled directly on transient retinal ganglion cells, neuromorphic event sensors ignore static backgrounds, tracking bullet-speed blades at microsecond latency across a million-fold light range on 25 milliwatts.
source: Lichtsteiner et al. 2008; Gallego et al. 2020
note: Silicon convergence on retinal temporal-difference coding.

milestone: Photovoltaic subretinal & V1 cortical visual prosthesis
species_or_system: PRIMA wireless subretinal microchip / intracortical V1 array
optical_type: AR infrared camera glasses -> 378-pixel wireless silicon subretinal photovoltaic array
opsin_class: Near-IR silicon photovoltaic pixels stimulating surviving bipolar cells
genetic_toolkit: Direct silicon-to-human-bipolar-neuron electrical synapse bridge
plain_title: Wireless two-millimeter silicon wafers restore letter reading in blind human maculas
plain_text: Beaming near-infrared patterns from camera glasses onto a hair-thin photovoltaic chip under a degenerated macula bypasses lost photoreceptors, letting formerly blind patients read letters again.
source: Palanker et al. 2020; Holz et al. 2024; Fernandez et al. 2021
note: First clinical silicon-to-retina prosthetic restoration of form vision.

species_or_system: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST at L2, 1.5M km)
optical_type: 18-segment 6,500-mm gold-coated beryllium three-mirror anastigmat at 40 K
opsin_class: 67M HgCdTe (NIR) & Si:As (MIRI at 6.7 K) single-photon detectors
genetic_toolkit: Active wavefront-sensing hexapod mirrors + 5-layer sunshield
plain_title: Humanity's giant scallop-style gold mirror sees galaxies 13.5 billion years away
plain_text: Orbiting 1.5 million kilometers from Earth and cooled to 6.7 kelvin, Webb's eighteen segmented mirrors resolve a penny from forty kilometers away and count single infrared photons emitted 300 million years after the Big Bang.
note: Planetary exosomatic apex of optical aperture, angular acuity (0.07 arcsec) and spectral span.
